```lean
by
  -- Use the fact that Icc is a multiset of elements between a and b inclusive
  -- and that adding c to each element preserves the order and structure
  -- We can use the property that map preserves the structure of the interval
  -- and that the interval is closed under addition
  rw [Multiset.map]
  have : Multiset.Icc (c + a) (c + b) = Multiset.map (fun x => c + x) (Multiset.Icc a b) :=
    by
      induction on (Multiset.Icc a b)
      case empty =>
        show Multiset.Icc (c + a) (c + b) = Multiset.map (fun x => c + x) ∅
        simp [Multiset.Icc, Multiset.map]
      case cons x xs =>
        have h1 : x = a := by rw [Icc.eq_iff.1 (Multiset.Icc.eq_iff.2 ⟨x, rfl⟩)]
        have h2 : xs = Multiset.Icc a b \ {x} := by rw [Icc.remove_singleton]
        have h3 : Multiset.map (fun x => c + x) (Multiset.Icc a b) = {c + x} ++ Multiset.map (fun x => c + x) xs :=
          by simp [Multiset.map, h2]
        have h4 : Multiset.Icc (c + a) (c + b) = {c + a} ++ Multiset.Icc (c + a) (c + b) \ {c + a} :=
          by simp [Multiset.Icc]
        have h5 : Multiset.Icc (c + a) (c + b) \ {c + a} = Multiset.Icc (c + (a + 1)) (c + b) :=
          by rw [Icc.remove_singleton]
        have h6 : Multiset.map (fun x => c + x) xs = Multiset.Icc (c + (a + 1)) (c + b) :=
          by rw [h2, h3, h4, h5]
        have h7 : {c + a} ++ Multiset.Icc (c + (a + 1)) (c + b) = Multiset.Icc (c + a) (c + b) :=
          by rw [Icc.add_singleton]
        show Multiset.Icc (c + a) (c + b) = Multiset.map (fun x => c + x) (Multiset.Icc a b)
        rw [h3, h4, h5, h6, h7]
  exact this
```
